title: hilvan learner model, format 5
description: Everything hilvan knows about one learner: each card with every answer behind it, the learner's own words, the voices they chose, the answers of the inventory, the breaks they took, the texts and books they read and the words they took from them. Material - packs, the lexicon - is not in it; everything keys on what outlives a reload of a pack: a formula's id, a word's lemma, a sentence's text. Written by `hilvan export` and GET /api/model, read by `hilvan import`.

$schema.description: The schema the file follows: this one.

format.description: The version of the file's shape. A change that would break a reader of this format is a new one.

as_of.description: The moment the model is told as of: when it was written, or an earlier one for a snapshot - the answers given by then, played through the scheduler again.

languages.description: The languages the learner has to do with. Every language named elsewhere in the file is listed here.

native.description: Whether it is the learner's own language. At most one is.

packs.description: The packs the learner was learning from, and their versions. A reader that has other versions loaded can still read the model: cards key on ids, not on rows.

cards.description: Every card that has been answered. A card never answered is new and carries nothing of the learner; a loaded pack makes those.

anchors.description: The one sentence each word is heard in, fixed by its first answer. A sentence nothing shows any more - no loaded pack, no text, no word taken from it - is dropped on import, and the word is heard in the first sentence it is met in until it is answered again.

own_words.description: Nouns and verbs from the learner's own life, substituted into the slots of the drill that take them.

language.description: The language being learnt that the word is of.

native.description: What it means, in the learner's own language.

target.description: As it is said in a sentence: "a car", "swim".

voices.description: The voice the learner chose for a language, where they chose one. A snapshot carries the voices chosen when it was written: a choice keeps no date.

voice.description: The engine's own id of the voice.

inventory.description: Every answer of the inventory, either way: the commonest words of the language, each asked once - do you know it? A yes is also a declared review on the word's card.

breaks.description: The breaks the learner took, the earliest first: stretches the schedule's clock stood still. A card's interval runs only in time outside a break, so one that spans a break comes back that much later; a break with no end lasts until the learner is back. Breaks do not overlap, only the last may lack an end, and none holds an answer the tutor asked for - one may start at the moment of the last answer, which is how an absence is counted afterwards.

until.description: When the learner was back; null while the break is going on.

texts.description: The texts the learner reads, the earliest added first: their own material, kept whole as chapters of paragraphs of sentences - a book's chapters as its source gives them, one chapter for anything else. A sentence a text shares with a pack is one sentence. The place in a text keeps no history: a snapshot of an earlier day carries the texts added by then, at the place the learner is now.

author.description: Who wrote it, as the book or the page names them; null where it does not.

source.description: The link it came from - a book of Project Gutenberg, an article of Wikipedia, a page; null for a text pasted or opened from a file.

format.description: How it came in: plain text, markdown or subtitles pasted or from a file; a web page; a Wikipedia article; an EPUB or FB2 book.

opened_at.description: When it was last opened; null for a text never opened.

paragraph.description: The paragraph the learner stopped at, through the whole text, from 0; one the text has.

finished_at.description: When the learner said they had read it; null until they do.

chapters.description: Its chapters in order: a book has the ones its source gives, anything else has one.

title.description: The chapter as the source names it; null where it names none.

paragraphs.description: Its paragraphs, each the sentences in it, in order.

picks.description: The words the learner took into the deck from a sentence they read, the earliest first. The sentence is one the word has been met in: it is asked and heard there, and it outlives the text it came from. A word is taken from a sentence once.

form.description: How the word is spelt there: "went" for go.

start.description: The character it starts at, counted in code points.

word.description: A word of a language: its code and its lemma, lowercase - en:house, en:i - or a phrase the deck learns as one word, its words one space apart: en:make a decision, en:turn off.

card.description: One card: what it schedules, where it stands, and the answers that put it there. Its state is what its answers leave when played through FSRS in order; the fields are kept so a reader need not replay to know it.

kind.description: formula: saying a formula, prompted in the learner's own language. formula-recognise: understanding it, prompted in the language being learnt. word: a word, asked in a sentence. pair: two words the learner typed one for the other, asked in sentences with the word left out.

subject.description: A formula's id, a word - en:house - or a pair: en:say|tell.

state.description: basted: answered, still loose. sewn: holding over long intervals. A card with answers is never new.

stability.description: FSRS: days until recall is predicted to fall to 90%.

difficulty.description: FSRS: how hard the card is for this learner, 1 to 10.

lapses.description: How many times it was forgotten once sewn.

review.description: One answer, and the card as it left it.

source.description: asked: the tutor asked and the learner answered. declared: the learner said they know it unasked - the inventory - which moves the card as an easy would and is not counted as an answer.

elapsed_days.description: Days since the answer before, as FSRS counted them.

duration_ms.description: How long the answer took, when the app measured it.

attempts.description: The turns typed for the answer, in order; empty for one that was not typed.

attempt.description: One typed turn, as the server read it.

prompt.description: What the learner read, in their own language.

expected.description: The right answer closest to what was typed.

typed.description: What the learner typed, as typed.

failure.description: formula: the formula's own pieces did not come. order: every word came, in the wrong order. word: the shape came, a word it carries did not. Null when the turn was right.

missed.description: The words of the answer that did not come.

swapped.description: The words typed in the place of others, read into lemmas: each the word that stood there and the word typed - ["en:tell", "en:say"] for said where told stood. What the confusion pairs are found from.

pair.description: Two words the learner confuses: the language, then the two lemmas in order, lowercase - en:say|tell.
